key_insight: MineNPC-Task provides a user-authored, play-derived benchmark and evaluation harness that tests memory-aware, mixed-initiative LLM agents in open-world Minecraft with machine-checkable validators and a bounded-knowledge policy to prevent out-of-world shortcuts.
problem_solved: Addresses the lack of realistic, reproducible benchmarks for evaluating long-horizon memory, planning, and mixed-initiative behavior in open-world environments where synthetic prompts often fail to capture human task structure and shortcuts can invalidate evaluations.
method: Elicit tasks from formative and summative co-play with expert human players to capture realistic objectives and dependencies.
Normalize elicited tasks into parametric templates with explicit preconditions and dependency structure for systematic variation and reuse.
Pair tasks with machine-checkable validators and enforce a bounded-knowledge policy that forbids out-of-world shortcuts, enabling fair automated evaluation of memory-aware agents.
impact: Enables AI/ML practitioners to evaluate and compare agents on realistic memory and mixed-initiative capabilities in a reproducible, grounded setting, improving development of robust long-horizon and interactive LLM agents.

paper_title: MineNPC-Task: Task Suite for Memory-Aware Minecraft Agents
paper_authors: Tamil Sudaravan Mohan Doss, Michael Xu, Sudha Rao, Andrew D. Wilson, Balasaravanan Thoravi Kumaravel
